## bioRxiv
An MCP server for accessing bioRxiv and medRxiv preprint servers.

This server provides:
- Tools: Search preprints, get preprint details, list subject categories
- Prompts: Analyze preprint methodology and findings

bioRxiv is a preprint server for biological sciences operated by Cold Spring
Harbor Laboratory. It hosts research manuscripts that have NOT undergone peer
review. This server wraps the official bioRxiv API to provide structured access
to preprint metadata, abstracts, and full-text PDFs.

TOOL SELECTION GUIDE:
• search_preprints: Find preprints by date range and/or subject category (no keyword, author, or full-text search) - primary discovery tool
• get_preprint: Get full details for a specific preprint by DOI
• get_categories: List available subject categories for filtering
• search_published_preprints: Find preprints that have been formally published in journals
• funder_search: Find preprints by funding source (NIH, etc.)
• get_statistics: Usage and submission statistics

MULTI-TOOL WORKFLOWS:
For comprehensive literature analysis:
1. Use search_preprints to find relevant preprints by date range and category
2. Use get_preprint for detailed information on promising results
3. Use search_published_preprints to check if preprints have been peer-reviewed and published
4. Use funder_search to identify research funding patterns in a field

For tracking research trends:
1. Use get_categories to identify relevant subject areas
2. Use search_preprints with date filters for recent activity
3. Use get_statistics to understand submission volumes

## Consensus
When presenting search results, you MUST cite papers inline using their numbered references from the tool result (e.g. [1], [2], [3]). When discussing findings, always attribute them to specific papers: 'Caffeine improves endurance performance [1] and reduces perceived exertion [3].' At the end of your response, list all cited papers as numbered references with their titles hyperlinked to the URLs from the tool result: [1] [Paper Title](url) (Authors, Year, Journal, Citations). Use the exact paper URLs from the tool result — do not modify, shorten, or regenerate them. Do not omit paper links or summarize results without citing specific papers. IMPORTANT: At the END of your response, you MUST include the sign-up, upgrade, or usage message from the tool result word-for-word. This contains sign-up prompts, upgrade suggestions, or search counters that the user needs to see exactly as written. Do not omit, shorten, or rephrase it. Batch at most 3 search calls at a time to avoid rate limits. If you receive a rate limit error, wait 30 seconds before retrying. Do NOT apply search filters (year_min, year_max, study_types, domain, human, sample_size_min, sjr_max, controlled, sjr_min, citation_min, open_access, country) unless the user explicitly requests them or clearly expresses intent to narrow results. If the user asks a research question without mentioning filtering criteria, call search with only the query parameter.

## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

## Gmail
This is an MCP server provided by Gmail API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Gmail.

## Google_Drive
This is an MCP server provided by Drive API. The server provides tools for developers to build LLM applications on top of Drive.

name: Guidebook CI

# THE single PR/push gate. Absorbs what used to be three overlapping workflows:
# ci.yml, audit.yml (Repo Integrity Audits) and research-contract.yml. Each had
# its own checkout, its own pip install, and its own hand-transcribed list of
# checks; the three lists — plus scripts/preflight.sh — disagreed about which
# checks exist.
#
# There is now no list of checks in this file. Every check lives in
# governance/check-registry.yaml and is invoked by scripts/run_checks.py, which
# preflight.sh also calls. Adding a check means editing the registry; it does not
# mean editing this workflow.
#
# GATING — "what kind of work is this?"
# -------------------------------------
# The `classify` job diffs the change, maps the touched paths to WORK KINDS
# (data / schema / synthesis / governance / render / tooling) and emits the set of
# batteries that have anything to do. Every other job gates on that.
#
# This replaces path filters written as
#     contains(github.event.pull_request.changed_files, 'data/')
# `changed_files` on the PR payload is an INTEGER — the count of changed files —
# so `contains(12, 'data/')` was always false and the schema, db_integrity and
# governance jobs never ran on ANY pull request. The symptom was recorded in
# CLAUDE.md §7; this is the cause. Those three jobs now run on the PRs that
# warrant them.
#
# WHAT CHANGED SEMANTICALLY (everything else is a like-for-like move)
#   - schema/db_integrity/governance actually gate PRs now.
#   - validate_evidence_state additionally fires on synthesis diffs, per the
#     2026-07-23 enforcement plan finding F2.
#   - validate_axes and validate_verification_consistency reach CI; they ran only
#     in preflight before, so CI never saw them.
#   - Newly-wired checks (matrix_consistency, audit_evidence_metadata,
#     pipeline_contract_audit) are ADVISORY, per the repo's shakedown norm. None
#     was promoted to blocking in the commit that first wired it.
#
# Levels are declared in the registry, not here: run_checks.py exits non-zero only
# when a `blocking` check fails, so `continue-on-error` is no longer needed and no
# longer sprinkled across job definitions where it was easy to lose track of.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

env:
  GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH: data/guidebook.db

jobs:

  classify:
    name: Classify change (work kinds → batteries)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    outputs:
      kinds: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.kinds }}
      batteries: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.batteries }}
      checks: ${{ steps.plan.outputs.checks }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Install PyYAML
        run: pip install PyYAML --quiet

      - name: Resolve the base commit to diff against
        id: base
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            BASE="${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}"
          else
            BASE="${{ github.event.before }}"
          fi
          # A new branch, a force-push, or workflow_dispatch can leave BASE unset
          # or all-zeros. Fall back rather than classify against nothing — a
          # silently-empty diff would select only the always-on checks and read as
          # a green run that checked almost nothing.
          if [ -z "$BASE" ] || [ "$BASE" = "0000000000000000000000000000000000000000" ] \
             || ! git cat-file -e "$BASE^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
            BASE=$(git rev-parse origin/main 2>/dev/null || git rev-parse HEAD~1)
            echo "Base unusable; falling back to $BASE"
          fi
          echo "base=$BASE" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Compute the check plan
        id: plan
        run: |
          # pipefail is load-bearing here, not boilerplate. This pipe is the single
          # point where the whole gating plan is produced, and it is the only place
          # in the workflow where a command's exit code passes through one. The
          # default shell is `bash -e {0}` with no pipefail, so without this line a
          # failing run_checks.py (bad registry, failed git diff) would be masked by
          # tee's 0: the step would pass with empty kinds/batteries outputs, every
          # battery job's `if:` would evaluate false, and the workflow would go
          # green having run nothing at all.
          set -euo pipefail
          python3 scripts/run_checks.py \
            --changed-from "${{ steps.base.outputs.base }}" \
            --print-plan | tee -a "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # Human-readable record of what this run will and will not check, so a
      # green build never has to be taken on trust about its own coverage.
      - name: Explain the plan (build log)
        run: |
          python3 scripts/run_checks.py \
            --changed-from "${{ steps.base.outputs.base }}" --explain --dry-run

      - name: Registry selftest (BLOCKING — the gate that guards the gates)
        run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --selftest

  syntax:
    name: Syntax (UTF-8, JSON, YAML)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',syntax,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11"}
      - run: pip install PyYAML --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery syntax --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  structure:
    name: Structure (BPC, cross-refs)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',structure,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11"}
      - run: pip install PyYAML --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery structure --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  data:
    name: Data layer (DB integrity, migration reproducibility, citation mining)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',data,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.12"}
      - run: pip install PyYAML --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery data --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  db-integrity:
    name: DB integrity (content checks)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',db_integrity,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.12"}
      - run: pip install PyYAML --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery db_integrity --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  tests:
    name: Tests (regression cover for the audit scripts)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',tests,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11"}
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery tests --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  schema:
    name: Schema (entity YAML, evidence state, populations, jurisdictions)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',schema,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11"}
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery schema --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  governance:
    name: Governance (decisions, doctrine recheck, adversarial use, contract)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',governance,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # History required. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-19: the original justification named
      # meta_work_freeze, which has since been retired and deleted. Depth 0 is still
      # correct, for a different reason — claims_docket.py is the remaining script in
      # this battery that shells out to git. Verified by scanning every governance
      # battery cmd for a git subprocess call rather than by trusting this comment.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: {fetch-depth: 0}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11"}
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery governance --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  attestation:
    name: Attestations (presence, schema, evidence, verdict)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',attestation,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # Full history required. RE-DERIVED 2026-08-19: the original justification was
      # check_2_doctrine_sha resolving each attestation's last-modifying commit — that
      # check was retired with the doctrine token, and check_7 states it is "not
      # history-depth sensitive". Depth 0 is retained because adherence_log_audit.py
      # still resolves changesets via git (--base/--head), and a shallow checkout would
      # scope the attestation gates to nothing — a gate examining zero subjects while
      # reporting PASS is this repo's signature failure.
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with: {fetch-depth: 0}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11"}
      - run: pip install PyYAML jsonschema --quiet
      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery attestation --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

  research:
    name: Research contract (definition-of-done + its enforcers)
    needs: classify
    if: contains(format(',{0},', needs.classify.outputs.batteries), ',research,')
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.12"}
      - run: pip install -r requirements.txt jsonschema --quiet

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with: {node-version: "20"}

      - run: python3 scripts/run_checks.py --battery render --kinds "${{ needs.classify.outputs.kinds }}" --github

    if: github.event_name == 'push'

        with: {fetch-depth: 2}
      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with: {python-version: "3.11"}

      - name: Commit message format
        run: python3 scripts/ci_helpers/check_commit_msg.py

name: Regenerate derived outputs

# Rebuilds every DB-derived output and commits the result back to main.
#
# Absorbs three near-identical workflows — regenerate-vetting-surface.yml,
# regenerate-evidentiary-audit.yml and regenerate-pipeline-completeness.yml —
# which differed only in the generator invoked, the files staged, the commit
# prefix and the trigger paths. Everything else (checkout, python, concurrency,
# the byte-identical short-circuit, the race-aware push retry) was copied three
# times, so a fix to the push retry had to be made three times or the copies
# drifted. That is now one matrix.
#
# WHAT MOVED OUT OF HERE
# ----------------------
# Two of the three old workflows also ran a `check` job on pull requests, failing
# if the committed output was stale versus the DB. That duty now belongs to
# ci.yml's `render` battery, which runs the same `--check` gates from
# governance/check-registry.yaml and is gated on the same work kinds. Keeping a
# second copy of the PR gate here would mean two places to keep in step. This
# workflow is now purely the write-back half.
#
# DETERMINISM / LOOP SAFETY
# -------------------------
# Each generator derives its "as-of" date from the DB's own max(updated_at), never
# wall-clock, so identical DB content produces byte-identical output. This
# workflow's own commits touch only generated files — never data/guidebook.db — so
# they cannot retrigger it. Belt and braces: each matrix leg exits without
# committing when its regenerated output is byte-identical to the committed copy.

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
    paths:
      - 'data/guidebook.db'
      - 'governance/pipeline-contract.yaml'
      - 'tools/evidentiary_audit.py'
      - 'tools/pipeline_completeness.py'
      - 'tools/regenerate_vetting_surface.py'
      - '.github/workflows/regenerate-derived.yml'
  schedule:
    # Mondays 07:30 UTC, after the weekly source-verification job. A belt-and-
    # braces catch; safe when nothing changed, per the loop-safety note above.
    - cron: '30 7 * * 1'
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  regenerate:
    name: ${{ matrix.name }}
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    # Per-leg concurrency: two legs write different files and must not be
    # serialised against each other, but a leg must not race itself.
    concurrency:
      group: regenerate-${{ matrix.id }}
      cancel-in-progress: false
    strategy:
      # One stale output must not stop the others from being refreshed.
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - id: vetting-surface
            name: Vetting surface
            generator: tools/regenerate_vetting_surface.py
            commit_prefix: vetting-surface-regen
            outputs: tools/spec-curation-vetting-surface.html

          - id: evidentiary-audit
            name: Evidentiary audit
            generator: tools/evidentiary_audit.py
            commit_prefix: evidentiary-audit-regen
            outputs: >-
              audits/evidentiary-base-audit.md
              audits/evidentiary-base-audit.csv
              audits/evidentiary-base-audit-items.csv
              audits/evidentiary-base-audit.json
              tools/evidentiary-audit-dashboard.html

          - id: pipeline-completeness
            name: Pipeline completeness
            generator: tools/pipeline_completeness.py
            commit_prefix: pipeline-completeness-regen
            outputs: tools/pipeline-completeness-dashboard.html

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 1

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.11'

      - name: Install deps
        run: pip install --quiet PyYAML

      # Call the writer; never redirect its stdout. The tools write their own
      # output path (DEFAULT_OUT), so `python3 tool.py > out.html` captures the
      # STATUS LINE instead of the HTML. That happened on 2026-07-24; the fix is
      # this comment plus never reintroducing the redirect.
      - name: Regenerate
        env:
          GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH: data/guidebook.db
        run: python3 ${{ matrix.generator }}

      - name: Commit if changed
        id: commit
        run: |
          set -e
          git config user.name  "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add ${{ matrix.outputs }}

          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "No changes to commit (output byte-identical to the committed copy)."
            echo "committed=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi

          TS=$(date -u '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M')
          git commit -m "${{ matrix.commit_prefix }}: rebuild after data change [${TS}]"
          echo "committed=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - name: Push with race-aware retry
        if: steps.commit.outputs.committed == 'true'
        run: |
          set -e
          for i in 1 2 3; do
            if git push origin main; then
              echo "Push succeeded on attempt $i"
              exit 0
            fi
            echo "Push attempt $i failed; pulling --rebase and retrying"
            git pull --rebase origin main || true
            sleep $((i * 5))
          done
          echo "All push attempts failed"
          exit 1

name: Source verification pipeline (V1.2)

# 6-phase pipeline per references/audits/verification-pipeline-proposal-2026-05-12-v2.md:
#   Phase 0  PMC extractor (no network)
#   Phase 1a PMID -> DOI via NCBI
#   Phase 1b PMCID -> DOI via NCBI
#   Phase 2a CrossRef structured (person-author academic)
#   Phase 2b CrossRef bibliographic (corporate-author academic)
#   Phase 3  CrossRef type:standard (ISO/EN/BSI/IEC/PAS standards)
#   Phase 4  CrossRef DOI-lookup metadata enrichment (V1.2 — fills pages,
#            pub_month, language, subtype, citation_count, ORCID, full author
#            lists; promotes metadata_quality AUTHOR-TITLE-ONLY → COMPLETE)
#
# State before/after and per-phase counts are written to the pipeline_runs table
# in data/guidebook.db — consistent with the project's SQLite-first tracking pattern.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      max_resolve:
        description: 'Max candidates per CrossRef phase (2a/2b/3)'
        required: false
        default: '500'
      skip_no_match_days:
        description: 'Days to skip NO-MATCH rows before retrying'
        required: false
        default: '30'
      rate_limit:
        description: 'Seconds between API calls'
        required: false
        default: '5.0'
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 6 * * 1'  # Mondays 06:00 UTC

# Prevent overlapping runs racing on data/guidebook.db.
concurrency:
  group: source-verification
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  resolve:
    name: Resolve DOIs and verify sources
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 360
    permissions:
      contents: write

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: '3.12'

      - name: Run verification pipeline
        env:
          GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH: data/guidebook.db
          MAX_RESOLVE: ${{ github.event.inputs.max_resolve || '500' }}
          SKIP_NO_MATCH_DAYS: ${{ github.event.inputs.skip_no_match_days || '30' }}
          RATE_LIMIT: ${{ github.event.inputs.rate_limit || '5.0' }}
        run: python scripts/resolve_dois.py

      - name: Build commit message from pipeline_runs
        id: msg
        run: |
          python - <<'PY'
          import sqlite3, os
          c = sqlite3.connect('data/guidebook.db')
          r = c.execute("""
              SELECT run_id, total_resolved,
                     doi_before, doi_after,
                     verified_before, verified_after,
                     pmcid_before, pmcid_after,
                     metadata_complete_before, metadata_complete_after,
                     phase_0_extracted,
                     phase_1a_resolved, phase_1b_resolved,
                     phase_2a_resolved, phase_2b_resolved,
                     phase_3_resolved,
                     phase_4_enriched, phase_4_complete,
                     phase_1a_transient + phase_1b_transient + phase_4_transient AS transient
              FROM pipeline_runs
              ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1
          """).fetchone()
          if not r:
              msg = "source-verification: V1.2 pipeline run — no run record found"
          else:
              (run_id, total, doi_b, doi_a, ver_b, ver_a, pmc_b, pmc_a,
               mc_b, mc_a,
               p0, p1a, p1b, p2a, p2b, p3, p4e, p4c, transient) = r
              doi_d = doi_a - doi_b
              ver_d = ver_a - ver_b
              pmc_d = pmc_a - pmc_b
              mc_d  = mc_a  - mc_b
              msg = (
                  f"source-verification: V1.2 run {run_id} — "
                  f"doi {doi_d:+d} ({doi_a} total), "
                  f"verified {ver_d:+d} ({ver_a} total), "
                  f"COMPLETE {mc_d:+d} ({mc_a} total), "
                  f"pmcid {pmc_d:+d} ({pmc_a} total); "
                  f"phases p0={p0} p1a={p1a} p1b={p1b} p2a={p2a} p2b={p2b} p3={p3} "
                  f"p4={p4e}({p4c}→COMPLETE)"
                  + (f"; {transient} transient" if transient else "")
              )
          print(msg)
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as f:
              f.write(f"msg={msg}\n")
          PY

      - name: Commit and push if changed
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add data/guidebook.db
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "No verification changes — nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "${{ steps.msg.outputs.msg }}"

          # Push with race-aware retry. The DB is a binary file — git cannot
          # auto-merge it, so a conflicting rebase indicates main has advanced
          # since our checkout and our work is now based on an obsolete state.
          # In that case we abandon this run's results and exit cleanly; the
          # next scheduled run will start from the new state and reprocess.
          for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            git fetch origin main
            if git rebase origin/main; then
              # No conflict — try to push.
              if git push origin main; then
                echo "Push succeeded on attempt $i"
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "Push attempt $i failed (non-conflict, likely transient); backing off..."
              sleep $((i * 5))
            else
              # Rebase conflict. Binary DB cannot auto-merge.
              # The run's results were computed against an obsolete DB state.
              # Discarding cleanly so the next run can start fresh.
              echo "Rebase conflict on data/guidebook.db: main advanced during this run."
              echo "Discarding this run's results; next scheduled run will reprocess."
              git rebase --abort 2>/dev/null || true
              git reset --hard origin/main
              exit 0
            fi
          done
          echo "ERROR: push failed after 5 transient retries"
          exit 1

name: URL verification (Channel 2 V1)

# Generic URL-fetch + title-match verifier per
#   scripts/verify_urls.py
#   references/audits/verification-pipeline-proposal-2026-05-12-v2.md §Channel 2
#
# Scope: sources with url IS NOT NULL AND verification_status IS NULL.
# Outcomes: VERIFIED / PROBABILISTIC / NO-MATCH (retry in 30d) / DEAD-LINK /
#           DEAD-DNS / WAYBACK-MATCH / transient (retry next run).
#
# State tracking: url_verification_runs table in data/guidebook.db.
# This is independent of pipeline_runs (used by Channel 1) — both channels can
# run concurrently without contention.

on:
  schedule:
    # Bi-weekly, complementing the weekly Channel 1 run. URLs change slowly;
    # less aggressive cadence avoids overloading publisher sites.
    - cron: "0 06 1,15 * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      max_verify:
        description: "Max URLs to attempt this run"
        required: false
        default: "500"
        type: string
      rate_limit:
        description: "Seconds between requests"
        required: false
        default: "3.0"
        type: string
      use_wayback:
        description: "Enable archive.org Wayback fallback on dead links"
        required: false
        default: "1"
        type: choice
        options:
          - "1"
          - "0"

concurrency:
  group: url-verification
  cancel-in-progress: false

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  verify:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 240
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Run URL verifier
        env:
          GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH:  data/guidebook.db
          MAX_VERIFY:         ${{ inputs.max_verify || '500' }}
          RATE_LIMIT:         ${{ inputs.rate_limit || '3.0' }}
          USE_WAYBACK:        ${{ inputs.use_wayback || '1' }}
          SKIP_NO_MATCH_DAYS: "30"
          GITHUB_RUN_ID:      ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          python scripts/verify_urls.py

      - name: Build commit message from url_verification_runs
        id: msg
        run: |
          python <<'PY'
          import sqlite3, os
          c = sqlite3.connect('data/guidebook.db')
          r = c.execute("""
              SELECT run_id, candidates_pool, attempted,
                     verified, probabilistic, no_match,
                     dead, wayback_verified, wayback_probabilistic,
                     dead_dns, transient,
                     verified_before, verified_after
              FROM url_verification_runs
              ORDER BY started_at DESC LIMIT 1
          """).fetchone()
          if not r:
              msg = "url-verification: no run record found"
          else:
              (run_id, pool, attempted, ver, prob, nm, dead, wv, wp, dns,
               trans, vb, va) = r
              ver_d = (va or 0) - (vb or 0)
              msg = (
                  f"url-verification: V1 run {run_id} — "
                  f"verified {ver_d:+d} ({va} total); "
                  f"attempted={attempted}/{pool}; "
                  f"outcomes V={ver} P={prob} NM={nm} D={dead} "
                  f"WV={wv} WP={wp} DNS={dns}"
                  + (f"; {trans} transient" if trans else "")
              )
          print(msg)
          with open(os.environ['GITHUB_OUTPUT'], 'a') as f:
              f.write(f"msg={msg}\n")
          PY

      - name: Commit and push if changed
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git add data/guidebook.db
          if git diff --cached --quiet; then
            echo "No verification changes — nothing to commit"
            exit 0
          fi
          git commit -m "${{ steps.msg.outputs.msg }}"

          # Push with binary-conflict-aware retry (same pattern as Channel 1).
          for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
            git fetch origin main
            if git rebase origin/main; then
              if git push origin main; then
                echo "Push succeeded on attempt $i"
                exit 0
              fi
              echo "Push attempt $i failed (transient); backing off..."
              sleep $((i * 5))
            else
              echo "Rebase conflict on data/guidebook.db: main advanced during run."
              echo "Discarding this run's results; next scheduled run will reprocess."
              git rebase --abort 2>/dev/null || true
              git reset --hard origin/main
              exit 0
            fi
          done
          echo "ERROR: push failed after 5 transient retries"
          exit 1

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# regenerate_derived.sh — regenerate every DB-derived output the CORRECT way, then verify.
#
# Lesson (2026-07-24): a dashboard was regenerated with `python3 tool.py > out.html`, which
# captured the tool's stdout STATUS LINE instead of its HTML — the tools write their own
# output path (DEFAULT_OUT). The `> redirect` is always wrong here; call the writer, no redirect.
# This script is the single sanctioned regeneration entry point after ANY data/guidebook.db change.
#
# Each generator writes its own file(s); we then run the tools' own `--check` gates (what CI runs)
# to prove the committed tree now matches a fresh regeneration. Exit non-zero if anything is stale.

python3 tools/pipeline_completeness.py
python3 tools/evidentiary_audit.py
python3 tools/regenerate_vetting_surface.py

echo "== Verifying --check gates (mirror CI regenerate-*.yml) =="
python3 tools/pipeline_completeness.py --check
python3 tools/evidentiary_audit.py --check

echo "All DB-derived outputs regenerated and --check-clean. Review 'git status' and commit."

1. Brief location: always `references/audit-briefs/{item_code}_brief.md`

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
graph_audit.py — vectorized structural audit (stdlib graph spine, data layer).

Builds a derived, read-only audit graph from data/guidebook.db and runs Tier-1
topology checks over it, unifying orphan / dangling-reference / empty-table /
state-distribution checks that today are scattered across skills and audit scripts.
It NEVER writes guidebook.db; the audit graph is a throwaway artifact.

Checks (data + code + content layers):
  1. orphan.dangling_citation     (ERROR) value-layer ref with no evidence_sources row
                                  — the vetting-surface `orphan_links` invariant; must be 0
  2. cycle.population_parent      (ERROR) populations.parent_code forms a cycle
  3. ref.dangling_structural      (ERROR) fk / self_ref / item-population junction edge to
                                  a missing node (items.bpc_source_slug, populations.parent_code,
                                  item_taxonomy_links) — corruption no other check covered
  4. orphan.uncited_source        (WARN)  evidence source cited by nothing
  5. ref.unresolved_conn_target   (WARN)  connection_target not resolving to item/slug
                                  (phantom-item vs unresolved-identifier)
  6. code.phantom_table           (WARN)  script SQL references a table absent from
                                  guidebook.db (dormant/stale/legacy query)
  7. ref.phantom_identifier       (WARN)  prose references an item/source/... identifier
                                  that resolves to no entity (candidate phantom ref)
  8. table.empty_mission_critical (INFO)  mission-critical table at/near 0 rows
                                  (suppressed against known_debt.yaml, warrant-checked)
  9. table.missing_mission_critical (WARN) mission-critical table ABSENT from the DB (dropped)
 10. connection.empty_description (INFO)  connections with empty description
 11. state.distribution           (INFO)  lifecycle CHECK-enum distributions
 12. graph.components             (INFO)  connected-component / island count

Every check ships with the `--selftest` mutation harness below (a verifier that has
only ever passed is unverified — integrity-protocol Mode 1 §3).

Exit code: 0 = no LIVE (non-known-debt) ERROR finding; 1 = at least one.

Usage:
    python3 scripts/audit/graph_audit.py
    python3 scripts/audit/graph_audit.py --selftest
    GUIDEBOOK_DB_PATH=/path/to/db python3 scripts/audit/graph_audit.py
"""
